headline: Federal slowdown weighs on revenue, cost cuts lift margin
summary_short: Booz Allen's revenue fell 4.2% y/y to $2.80 billion as slowed federal procurement cut headcount and billable expenses, but cost discipline lifted operating income 8.6% to $279 million; net income fell 26.9% to $198 million on a higher effective tax rate, with diluted EPS of $1.63 vs $2.16 a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue declined 4.2% y/y on slowed U.S. government procurement, which reduced headcount and billable expenses. Cost of revenue fell 6% (lower headcount costs, no repeat of a $30M prior-year severance charge), lifting operating margin to 10% from 9% and operating income 8.6% to $279M. Net income fell 26.9% to $198M as the effective tax rate rose to 21.1% from -25.5% (a prior-year tax-reserve release didn't recur). Diluted EPS was $1.63 vs $2.16. Operating cash flow rose to $281M from $119M on working-capital management and lower taxes. The company closed the $235M Defy Security acquisition; backlog was $39.48B, +3% y/y. Cash fell to $540M. No forward guidance stated.

drivers.explanation: Decline was primarily driven by the impact of slowed procurement, which reduced headcount and billable expenses.
Cost cuts across cost of revenue, billable expenses, and G&A (mostly headcount-related, plus no repeat of a prior-year severance charge) outpaced the revenue decline.
The tax-expense increase was primarily driven by an increase in pre-tax income and a decrease in the uncertain-tax-position reserve versus a year earlier that did not recur.
Move tracks the operating-income gain plus higher other income (investment fair-value gains) and higher D&A from the Defy Security acquisition.

Management points to a slower federal procurement environment and policy uncertainty (FAR reform, fixed-price contracting push) as the backdrop, offset by cost discipline and continued M&A (Defy Security closed; Ultra Mission Solutions pending).
